justification: All four issues from round 1 (two critical, two minor) are fixed, and I re-verified every fix against the live source rather than trusting the diff. (1) The PostgreSQL tutorial quote in the 'Commit after an ignored error' exercise now reads 'ROLLBACK TO is the only way to regain control of a transaction block that was put in aborted state by the system due to an error, short of rolling it back completely and starting again.' -- fetching tutorial-transactions.html live returns the identical sentence verbatim (the article drops only the leading 'Moreover,' which is a normal, non-distorting quote-start trim); the inverted-emphasis bracketed edit from round 1 is gone. (2) The WAL section now quotes 'because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of readers, writers and readers can run at the same time' and, separately, 'readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers' -- fetching wal.html live confirms both are verbatim sentences from the page (the first from the body text, the second from the advantages list), and 'permits'/'simultaneous' -- the words that gave away the round-1 splice -- no longer appear anywhere in the article's WAL quotes. (3) The Repeatable Read quote is now the complete sentence, 'a query in a repeatable read transaction sees a snapshot as of the start of the first non-transaction-control statement in the transaction, not as of the start of the current statement within the transaction,' which live transaction-iso.html confirms verbatim -- no more silently truncated quotation marks. (4) The isolation table's introduction no longer calls it 'the standard's own table'; it now says PostgreSQL's documentation 'presents this as a table of what the standard permits at each level, adapted here to the three anomalies above (PostgreSQL's own version of the table adds a fourth column for the serialization anomaly, covered separately below)' and the following paragraph correctly attributes the 'Allowed, but not in PG' cells to PostgreSQL's own table -- live transaction-iso.html confirms Table 13.1 really is captioned as showing 'the SQL standard and PostgreSQL-implemented transaction isolation levels' together with exactly those two 'Allowed, but not in PG' cells (Read Uncommitted/Dirty Read and Repeatable Read/Phantom Read), so the article's revised framing is now honest about what was adapted versus reproduced. I also spot-checked, live, several quotes the round-1 critic had already cleared and that the diff shows were untouched or only lightly retouched in this round: the SQL Server 'is the SQL Server default' / shared-locks / READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT-on-Azure sentences (verbatim on learn.microsoft.com), the SQL Server deadlock guide's T1/T2 shared-lock-cycle example, lock-monitor-thread and 'chooses one of the tasks as a victim and terminates its transaction with an error' sentences (verbatim), the SQLite isolation.html 'all transactions in SQLite show "serializable" isolation... actually serializing the writes... single writer at a time' sentence (verbatim), and a fifth quote this round's diff shows was also corrected beyond the four the round-1 review flagged: the deadlock-guide quote in the retry-logic paragraph changed from an ellipsis-spliced 'terminates the current batch... rolls back the transaction of the deadlock victim, and returns error 1205' to the full, verbatim 'terminates the current batch, rolls back the transaction, and returns error 1205 to the application' -- a good-faith tightening beyond what this critic flagged, and it now matches the source exactly. `node tools/run-code.mjs` still passes (26 blocks, 14 executed). On a fresh full read: the two-real-connection SQLite demos remain the genuine differentiator this pillar needed -- no dirty read, the RESERVED-vs-EXCLUSIVE commit block, the WAL snapshot demo, and the reproducible two-thread SQLite lock-cycle using Barrier/ManualResetEventSlim are not something a typical 'ACID explained' page does, and the article is still explicit that its own shared-connection `sql run` blocks cannot show any of this -- honest scoping, not overclaiming what SQLite/the harness can demonstrate. Heading structure (a run of specific questions, no Introduction/Conclusion/Exercises boilerplate) is visibly different from both sibling databases articles' declarative-statement headings, which is real structural variation rather than a repeated template. No filler openers, no restated title, no keyword stuffing, no ad code or ad placeholders anywhere in the file. Sourcing hygiene is now clean across every quotation I checked (9 fetched pages, both this round and carried over from round 1's clearance of the other nine fragments) -- nothing fabricated, spliced, or mis-captioned remains that I could find. This is not a 10: the differentiator is strong but narrow (four isolation/concurrency demos, not new territory beyond what the plan called for), and a couple of the SQLite lock-state explanations (e.g., the RESERVED/EXCLUSIVE escalation paragraph) ask a first-time reader to hold a fair amount of mechanism in their head without a diagram, which is a minor depth-vs-accessibility tradeoff rather than a policy problem. Nothing here caps the score.
